evals.prompt: Describe assignments only; do not dispatch agents or edit files. Two independent component tasks own disjoint source files but both will edit docs/file-map.md and docs/known-issues.md. Explain which work can run in parallel and which edits must be serialized.
evals.expected_output: Run independent component work in parallel, but serialize edits to each shared document so workers do not edit the same file concurrently.
assertions: Independent source work can run in parallel.
Edits to each shared file are serialized.

evals.prompt: Describe coordination only; do not dispatch agents or edit files. Task A owns a parser and its area documentation. Task B owns an independent report formatter and its area documentation. Task C needs the completed parser from A. No files overlap. Explain the dispatch waves and execution mode while the user remains in conversation.
evals.expected_output: Run A and B in parallel background subagents, then start C after A completes. Keep the coordinator available for active dialogue.
assertions: A and B can run in parallel without serializing disjoint documentation.
C waits for A rather than dispatching with an unmet dependency.
Uses background subagents and keeps the coordinator available to the user.

evals.prompt: Describe assignments and communication only; do not dispatch agents or write files. Three implementation tasks need the same large-log investigation. A research note and a previous commit already provide most context. Explain how to fill the remaining gap and share findings without repeated investigation or copying the full context into every message. Include a draft exploration brief with the available context pointers, acceptance criteria and known negative cases; mark details not supplied as unresolved.
evals.expected_output: Use one exploration subagent for the shared gap, reuse the existing note and commit, and communicate concise results through accessible context pointers.
assertions: Proposes one shared exploration rather than three duplicate investigations.
Reuses the existing research note and commit through context pointers.
Keeps communication sparse rather than forwarding complete logs or repeated context.

evals.prompt: Describe dispatch preparation only; do not dispatch or write files. One task is bounded read-only exploration; another is a substantive cross-file code review. The router instructions have already been loaded for the first task and remain in context for the second. All required task facts and runtime capabilities are available. Explain routing, how model and effort reach dispatch, and how runtime limits are chosen. Include draft dispatch records showing the proposed model, effort, runtime limit, deadline and enforcement state; leave unavailable concrete values unresolved and do not claim dispatch or arming occurred.
evals.expected_output: Load subagent-model-router once per agent context, evaluate a distinct route for each materially different subtask, submit model and effort policy through dispatch controls (explicit effort when required, otherwise omit effort), and assign each worker an effort-appropriate runtime limit.
assertions: Routes the exploration and substantive review as materially different subtasks.
Reuses already available router instructions rather than loading them again for the second task.
Submits the exact routed model and reasoning effort through dispatch controls.
Assigns every subagent a runtime limit based on expected effort and complexity.
Omits effort for bounded exploration and applies explicit effort only to substantive review; risk tier alone does not create an effort requirement.

evals.prompt: Describe procedure only; do not dispatch or write files. The user requires approval before dispatch. All task facts are available and no model preference was given. A proposed worker wants to spawn helpers, but nested delegation has not been authorized. Explain routing, the approval boundary, and the worker delegation policy.
evals.expected_output: Route using subagent-model-router without soliciting a model preference, honor the requested approval before dispatch, and prohibit nested delegation unless intentionally authorized.
assertions: Uses the router to select exact model and effort without asking the user to choose them.
Honors the explicit pre-dispatch approval boundary.
Prohibits nested delegation unless intentionally authorized.

evals.prompt: Describe coordination only; do not dispatch, send messages, or write files. A background worker reaches its initial deadline while still running, with no prior extension. Describe the immediate request and deadline. The worker replies in time with status, completed work, blockers, and an ETA; explain the available decisions and the records needed if it continues.
evals.expected_output: Request the four-part checkpoint by a bounded response deadline. A timely response permits confirming completion, stopping, or granting at most one ETA-based extension; a grant increments the count, records a deadline, and rearms enforcement.
assertions: Requests status, completed work, blockers, and an updated ETA by a bounded checkpoint deadline.
A timely checkpoint leads to confirmation of completion, stopping, or at most one ETA-based extension.
If an extension is granted, increments the count, records the new deadline, and rearms enforcement.

evals.prompt: Give an execution decision only; do not execute tools, dispatch agents, or edit files. The delegate-to-subagents workflow is active. A ready task is a one-line documentation edit with a known check, and the coordinator already has the context. No user restriction prevents delegation. Choose the executor and describe communication and dispatch settings. Include a draft dispatch record with the selected model, effort, deadline and enforcement state; mark unavailable values unresolved and do not claim dispatch or arming occurred.
evals.expected_output: Delegate the documentation implementation task, use sparse context pointers, submit the router-selected model and effort policy with a runtime limit, and omit effort when the task does not require it.
assertions: Assigns the task to a subagent rather than choosing local execution because it is cheaper.
Uses sparse communication and context pointers.
Uses the router-selected exact model and effort with a runtime limit.
Records host_default omission instead of inventing an effort value for ordinary documentation implementation.

evals.prompt: Describe executor choices only; do not run tools, dispatch, edit files, or commit. The delegate-to-subagents workflow is active. The parent coordinator has all context needed for a read-only Git status check and a deterministic commit of verified, explicitly authorized changes. Choose the executor for each operation under the active skill. Then explain what changes if the user says not to commit yet, or if unexpected files make commit scope uncertain.
evals.expected_output: Assign both the status check and the safe, authorized deterministic commit to subagents under the all-work-in-subagents rule, even though the parent has the context. A no-commit instruction blocks committing by every agent. Unexpected files require resolving scope before any commit; delegation does not authorize uncertain or unsafe commits.
assertions: Assigns both deterministic operations to subagents rather than direct parent execution.
Honors an explicit no-commit instruction for every agent.
Resolves uncertain commit scope before committing rather than treating delegation as authorization.

evals.prompt: Describe the parent's observable coordination actions only; do not dispatch or write files. Two background assignments are being started, with different effort estimates and deadlines. The parent intends to wait for updates; a blocking operation could outlast the earlier deadline. One worker then completes on time. State the records, monitoring setup and wait bound, handling of the blocking operation, and completion cleanup. Present a simulated fieldwise action log and records for both assignments, marking unknown values unresolved; do not claim any monitoring was actually armed.
evals.expected_output: For each assignment record identifiers, start, effort-based deadline, zero extensions and enforcement entry; arm monitoring before waiting, bound waits by the earliest deadline and independently time out blocking operations, and cancel the finished assignment's enforcement.
assertions: Records each assignment or task ID, agent ID, start, effort-based deadline, initial zero extension count, and enforcement handle or scheduler entry.
Arms parent-side enforcement before waiting and bounds the wait by the nearest active deadline.
Independently times out an operation that would prevent enforcement.
Cancels enforcement for the on-time completed assignment while continuing to monitor the other.

evals.prompt: Describe actions only; do not dispatch or send messages. Consider two separate running assignments. A receives no checkpoint by its response deadline. B received one ETA-based extension after a timely checkpoint; follow-up messages arrived, and its extended deadline now expires. For each, state the immediate action, whether another extension is allowed, and what must precede any replacement. For each assignment, include a simulated action log through the decision about replacement, including any routing and conditions needed before replacement.
evals.expected_output: Stop A when its checkpoint deadline passes and stop B when the extension expires; follow-up messages cannot reset the count or grant a second extension. Confirm the worker and associated write-producing operations stopped before transferring ownership and dispatching a fresh routed replacement.
assertions: Stops A when the bounded checkpoint response is absent or late.
Stops B at its extended deadline without granting a second extension or resetting the count for follow-up messages.
Confirms both the worker and associated write-producing operations stopped before ownership transfer and a fresh routed replacement.

evals.prompt: Describe actions only; do not dispatch or write files. After a user interruption, the parent regains control. One overdue worker has been told to stop but its write operation may still be running; a separate completed worker is available for a new independent assignment. Explain deadline checks, the unresolved worker's ownership, useful independent work, and monitoring state for the reused worker's new assignment. Include a draft record for the new assignment and a simulated action log; mark unknown values unresolved and do not claim any enforcement or dispatch occurred.
evals.expected_output: Recheck deadlines on return, report the unconfirmed stop and keep ownership exclusive while continuing independent authorized work. Treat the reused agent's new assignment separately, with its own identifiers, start, deadline, zero extension count and armed enforcement.
assertions: Rechecks active deadlines after the interruption when control returns.
Reports the unconfirmed stop and does not transfer ownership or dispatch overlapping work while the worker or its writes may continue.
Continues independent authorized work without claiming the blocked work completed.
Creates and arms a fresh runtime record for the reused agent's new assignment, including a zero extension count.

evals.prompt: Describe dispatch preparation only; do not dispatch or write files. A task is ordinary coding with no explicit effort request. The user explicitly chooses an exact model whose catalog tier is below the router recommendation. Host model control is supported, permitted, and live acceptance is confirmed. Explain model choice, effort argument, recorded route, and deadline handling.
evals.expected_output: Honor the exact user-chosen model over the advisory tier, while applying host controls and the task-based host_default effort policy. Omit effort, record the choice and policy, and preserve the runtime deadline.
assertions: Uses the exact user-selected model instead of enforcing the advisory tier.
Uses host_default and omits effort for ordinary coding.
Preserves host restrictions and runtime deadline enforcement.
Does not treat the router recommendation as user selection.

evals.prompt:
Apply the delegate-to-subagents skill to three assignments. Do not dispatch or edit files.

A: An already dispatched agent has all task context required by the subtask and its exact model matches the final route. The route is host_default, and the agent was originally spawned without an effort override.

B: The existing agent matches the final route model and effort policy but lacks task context required by the subtask; no other current agent has that context.

C: An existing agent has the task context and same model as the final host_default route, but its original spawn specified explicit effort.

For each assignment, explain whether you would use the existing agent or dispatch a fresh one.
evals.expected_output: Prefer the existing agent for A because context and route eligibility match. Dispatch a fresh agent for B because no existing agent has the needed context. Dispatch a fresh agent for C because its original explicit effort makes it ineligible for a host_default route despite matching model and context.
assertions: Prefers reuse of an existing context-bearing agent when exact route eligibility matches.
Chooses a fresh agent when no existing agent has required task context.
Rejects an agent with an original effort override for host_default reuse, even when model and context match.

pilot_harness.scope: offline maintained preparation and evidence grading; live runs need separate authorization
